channel.title: CTV News – Queen's Park
channel.description: Queen's Park coverage from CTV News Toronto.

item.title: ‘The clock is ticking:’ Ontario woman says she was denied coverage for drug to treat her rare cancer
TDSB trustees demand ‘clear and transparent’ criteria to get authority back
item.description: The dozen trustees who represent the Toronto District School Board are pushing for a meeting with Education Minister Paul Calandra to discuss how and when board supervision will end.

item.title: Ontario looking to amend the Fire Code amid rise of fires involving e-bikes and e-scooters
item.description: Ontario is proposing to ban storing electric bikes and electric scooters in hallways of condos and apartments amid a rise in lithium-ion battery fires.

item.title: The Ford government sent this doctor a letter over the ‘high number’ of days he worked. He wants an apology
item.description: A family doctor in Madoc, Ont. is speaking out about an “intimidating” letter he says that he received from the Ministry of Health questioning the “high number” of days he worked over the last year.

item.title: Ontario Liberal leadership hopefuls talk taxes, affordability and Doug Ford in final debate
item.description: Ontario Liberal leadership hopefuls are pitching themselves as the antidote to Premier Doug Ford in the final debate before voting begins with little disagreement between them, though several took different tacks on taxes.

item.title: Ford says OSAP auditors will clear low-risk career colleges first; no timeline given
item.description: An audit firm that is investigating student financial aid usage at Ontario career colleges is making it a priority to clear lower-risk schools first so their funding can be unfrozen, Premier Doug Ford said Wednesday, but he was not clear on a timeline.

item.title: Doug Ford weighs in on calls for Ontario to scrap seasonal time changes. Here is what he said
item.description: Ontario Premier Doug Ford says he is “very open” to eliminating seasonal time changes across the province, provided Quebec and neighbouring U.S. jurisdictions are on board.

item.title: Toronto wants a new deal with the province. Doug Ford says the answer is ‘no’
item.description: Ontario Premier Doug Ford says the province will not be hammering out a so-called “New Deal 2.0” to solve Toronto’s finances.

item.title: What elected trustees at supervised school boards can and can’t do, according to this memo
item.description: A leaked memo obtained by CTV News details the very limited roles and responsibilities of school trustees for the Toronto District School Board, the Toronto Catholic District School Board, and six other boards under supervision.

item.title: Ontario won’t make career college OSAP audit public, minister says
item.description: Ontario’s colleges and universities minister said Tuesday he will not be releasing a government-commissioned audit into student financial aid usage at career colleges.

item.title: Thousands of OSAP applications came from a single IP address, ministry alleges
item.description: At two career colleges now under the Ontario government’s microscope, more than half of the thousands of student financial aid applications last year came from a single IP address, officials allege in documents filed in court.

item.title: Toronto cyclists protest Ontario's bike lane removals at Queen's Park
item.description: Dozens of cycling advocates and protesters spent their Halloween decrying Ontario’s contentious decision to continue removing bike lanes across Toronto.

item.title: Ontario deficit grows to $16.9 billion as trade war with U.S. drags on
item.description: Ontario’s deficit has grown by more than $3 billion in the past few months as the province continues to face economic headwinds blowing up from the U.S.

item.title: Assault charges dropped against Sault MPP
item.description: More than a year after Sault Ste. Marie MPP Chris Scott was charged with two counts of assault, the case was dropped Wednesday.

item.title: Ontario environment minister hopes to burn more garbage for energy, build more landfills
item.description: Ontario’s environment minister hopes to burn more garbage for energy and build more landfills as the province runs out of space to dump its trash and is framing it as a way to fight U.S. President Donald Trump’s recent tariff on Canadian trash.
